newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso dismisses criticism of CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso dismisses criticism of CVRD sale.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said Friday he had yet to hear a convincing argument against the upcoming $5.0 billion privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
"All this stuff about CVRD is political. I've not yet heard a single technical argument (against the privatization)," Cardoso said in an interview on national CBN radio.
"I used to be against the privatization of Vale until I heard the arguments (in favor) which convinced me," he said.
The government is due to auction between 40 and 45 percent of CVRD's voting capital April 29 in the first stage of what is set to become Latin America's biggest privatization to date.
Parties from the left and center of Brazil's political spectrum oppose the sale, mostly on the grounds that CVRD's massive iron ore reserves represent a "strategic" interest for the nation.
Brazil's Catholic Church has also asked for the privatization to be suspended on what it said was ethical grounds.
But Cardoso brushed aside the criticism.

"What does Vale do that is strategic? It gets stones in Carajas (a mine site in the Amazon), puts them in a wagon, ships them to the port and away. That's what iron ore mining is all about. It's a basic activity," the president told CBN.
